overall_assessment: The codebase shows a solid foundation for the ExpenseTrack application with proper modular structure and alignment with the PRD and architecture. However, critical security and functional gaps in authentication and authorization logic prevent it from being production-ready. Several high-severity issues must be addressed before deployment.

bugs.description: The login endpoint returns a plain text password in the response body.
bugs.suggested_fix: Remove 'password' from the response model and ensure no sensitive data is ever returned in API responses.

bugs.description: Expense creation endpoint does not validate category against predefined list (Food, Transport, etc.) as required by PRD.
bugs.suggested_fix: Add category validation using a predefined enum or list before saving to database.

bugs.description: Update and delete expense endpoints do not verify that the requesting user owns the expense, creating a serious authorization flaw.
bugs.suggested_fix: Add ownership check by comparing expense.user_id with current_user.id before allowing modification.

bugs.description: Password hashing uses SHA-256 instead of bcrypt as specified in PRD and security requirements.
bugs.suggested_fix: Replace SHA-256 with bcrypt or equivalent adaptive hashing algorithm like Argon2.

bugs.description: Report endpoints do not filter data by authenticated user, risking data leakage.
bugs.suggested_fix: Ensure all report queries are scoped to request.user.id.

test_cases.description: Verifies that login response does not include password
Ensures only valid categories can be used when creating expenses
Prevents users from deleting expenses they don't own

bugs.description: JWT tokens are stored in localStorage which is vulnerable to XSS attacks.
bugs.suggested_fix: Use httpOnly cookies for token storage or implement secure in-memory storage with proper cleanup.

bugs.description: Date field does not default to current date as specified in PRD acceptance criteria.
bugs.suggested_fix: Set default value of date input to new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0] on component mount.

test_cases.description: Verifies that the date field defaults to current date
Ensures category field uses predefined valid options

recommendations: Immediately fix the password exposure in login response
Add user ownership checks on all expense operations
Validate expense category against allowed list
Store JWT tokens securely using httpOnly cookies
Ensure report endpoints are scoped to current user
Add comprehensive error handling in API routes
Implement input validation on both frontend and backend
